bounded_statement: The report's selected result claims to be the confirmed transit detection rate for the complete planned set of 40 candidate light curves (the domain declared by both the task and the report's own Scientific target section), but the rate is computed as 12/32 = 37.500 percent using only the 32 curves retained after photometric screening as the denominator. Computed over the declared complete-domain denominator of 40, the same event count yields 30.000 percent, so the retained-subset rate overstates the complete-domain rate by 7.5 percentage points while being labeled as the complete-domain rate, with no protocol amendment or approved deviation (the report itself states none exists).

counterevidence_considered.description: Strongest counterargument I tested: the report transparently discloses that the exposure denominator is the 32 retained curves, so a careful reader could recover the mismatch. However, disclosure does not repair the claim itself: the tagged selected result still asserts that 37.500 percent is the detection rate 'for the complete planned set of 40', and the report affirms no amendment redefined the target, so the headline claim remains a retained-subset rate presented for the complete domain.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: denominator disclosed but claim domain unchanged

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the demonstrated-issue verdict three ways. First, I checked whether any language in the report rescopes the selected result to the retained subset (e.g., a lower-bound or subset-only framing as in a correctly bounded report); there is none — the selected result and the scope section both assert the rate is 'of the complete planned set of 40'. Second, I checked whether an amendment or approved deviation could legitimize a retained-subset denominator for the complete-domain claim; the report explicitly states none exists. Third, I recomputed from the raw data to rule out a labeling typo: 32 retained and 12 detections are correct, so 12/32 = 37.500 percent is genuinely the retained-subset rate, and the complete-domain rate under the declared target would be 12/40 = 30.000 percent. All three attempts failed to overturn the verdict.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py computes the selected rate with the retained-subset count as the denominator (rate = percent(events, n_retained), 12/32) while the report text labels that rate as the detection rate 'for the complete planned set of 40 candidate light curves', producing a domain/denominator mismatch in the headline claim.
